The fix is to use `Math.round` when converting prices to cents. Let me fix all three places where this conversion happens:

content.text:
Fixed! The issue was floating-point precision in the price-to-cents conversion. When JavaScript multiplies 39.95 × 100, it can get 3995.0000000000005 instead of exactly 3995. Using `Math.round()` on the result ensures we always get whole cents.

I've updated three price conversion functions to use `Math.round()`:
- `parseEuros()` in money.js
- `cellCents()` in money.js  
- `decimalCommaToCents()` in locale.js

All tests pass and your gym membership now adds successfully.
